title.zh: 卷一百三十 列傳第八十: 王璵 李泌 崔造 關播
title.en: Volume 130 Biographies 80: Wang Yu, Li Bi, Cui Zao, Guan Bo
title.raw: 卷一百三十 列傳第八十: 王璵 李泌 崔造 關播 Volume 130 Biographies 80: Wang Yu, Li Bi, Cui Zao, Guan Bo

sentences.zh: 王玙 道士李國禎附

translations.literal: Wang Yu; appended: the Daoist Li Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu; with an appended biography of the Daoist Li Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 李泌 子繁 顧況附

translations.literal: Li Bi; appended: his son Fan and Gu Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi; with appended biographies of his son Fan and Gu Kuang.

sentences.zh: 崔造 關播 李元平附

translations.literal: Cui Zao; Guan Bo; appended: Li Yuanping.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao and Guan Bo; with an appended biography of Li Yuanping.

sentences.zh: 王玙，少習禮學，博求祠祭儀注以干時。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, from youth studied ritual learning, and broadly sought sacrificial protocols and regulations to advance by the times.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu studied ritual learning from his youth and assiduously collected sacrificial protocols and regulations in hopes of winning favor at court.

sentences.zh: 開元末，玄宗方尊道術，靡神不宗。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era, Emperor Xuanzong was then honoring Daoist arts, and there was no spirit he did not revere.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Kaiyuan reign, Emperor Xuanzong was exalting Daoist practices, and no deity went unhonored.

sentences.zh: 玙抗疏引古今祀典，請置春壇，祀青帝於國東郊，玄宗甚然之，因遷太常博士、侍御史，充祠祭使。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a memorial citing ancient and modern sacrificial canons, requesting establishment of a spring altar to sacrifice to the Green Emperor at the eastern suburb of the capital; Emperor Xuanzong greatly approved, and therefore promoted him to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attending Censor, and appointed him Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized the throne, citing sacrificial precedents old and new, and asked that a spring altar be established to worship the Green Emperor in the eastern suburbs of the capital. Xuanzong strongly approved; Yu was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Attending Censor and made Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.

sentences.zh: 玙專以祀事希幸，每行祠禱，或焚紙錢，禱祈福祐，近於巫覡，由是過承恩遇。

translations.literal: Yu specialized in using sacrificial affairs to seek favor; whenever he performed temple prayers he would sometimes burn paper money and pray for blessings and protection, approaching the ways of shamans, and thereby received excessive imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu made sacrificial business his path to favor. Whenever he conducted rites and prayers he would burn spirit money and plead for divine protection—conduct close to shamanism—and so won extravagant favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，累遷太常卿，以祠禱每多賜賚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Yu was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and because of his temple prayers he often received many gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong came to the throne, Yu rose in stages to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and received frequent largesse for his ritual prayers.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年七月，兼蒲州刺史，充蒲、同、絳等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Qianyuan, he was concurrently made Prefect of Pu and Military Commissioner of Pu, Tong, Jiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyuan 3 (760), he was also appointed Prefect of Pu and Military Commissioner over Pu, Tong, Jiang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔圓罷相，乃以玙為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Cui Yuan was removed from the chancellorship, Yu was then made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Cui Yuan left office, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 人物時望，素不為眾所稱，及當樞務，聲問頓減。

translations.literal: As a man his contemporary reputation had never been praised by the multitude, and once he held pivotal duties his renown abruptly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He had never enjoyed much esteem among his contemporaries, and once he took up the levers of power his reputation fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 玙又奏置太一神壇於南郊之東，請上躬行祀事。

translations.literal: Yu again memorialized to establish an altar to the Great One Spirit east of the southern suburb altar, and requested that the emperor personally perform the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu further proposed erecting an altar to the Great Unity Spirit east of the southern suburban altar and asked that the emperor perform the rites in person.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘗不豫，太卜云：「崇在山川。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong once fell ill, and the Grand Diviner said: "The affliction lies in mountains and rivers."
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong fell ill, the Grand Diviner declared, "The malady stems from mountains and rivers."

sentences.zh: 」玙乃遣女巫分行天下，祈祭名山大川。

translations.literal: Yu then dispatched shamankesses to travel throughout the realm in separate parties to pray and sacrifice at famous mountains and great rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then sent shamankesses throughout the empire to offer prayers and sacrifices at famous mountains and great rivers.

sentences.zh: 巫皆盛服乘傳而行，上令中使監之，因緣為奸，所至干托長吏，以邀賂遺。

translations.literal: The shamankesses all traveled in splendid dress riding relay horses; the emperor ordered palace envoys to supervise them, who used the opportunity for wickedness, and wherever they went they importuned senior officials to solicit bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The shamankesses traveled in grand attire on relay horses while palace envoys supervised them; both parties abused their posts, importuning local officials for bribes wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 一巫盛年而美，以惡少年數十自隨，尤為蠹弊，與其徒宿於黃州傳舍。

translations.literal: One shamankess in the prime of life and beautiful, with several tens of wicked youths following her, was especially corrupt; she and her followers lodged at the relay station in Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: One young and beautiful shamankess traveled with several dozen rowdy youths and was especially abusive; she and her band lodged at the Huangzhou relay station.

sentences.zh: 刺史左震晨至，驛門扃鐍，不可啟，震破鎖而入，曳女巫階下斬之，所從惡少年皆斃。

translations.literal: Prefect Zuo Zhen arrived in the morning; the relay gate was bolted shut and could not be opened; Zhen broke the lock and entered, dragged the shamankess down the steps and beheaded her, and all the wicked youths who followed were killed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Prefect Zuo Zhen found the station gate bolted shut. He broke the lock, dragged the shamankess down the steps and executed her, and killed all her rowdy followers as well.

sentences.zh: 閱其贓賂數十萬，震籍以上聞，仍請贓錢代貧民租稅，其中使發遣歸京，肅宗不能詰。

translations.literal: Examining her bribes of several hundred thousand, Zhen registered them and reported upward, and further requested that the illicit money substitute for poor people's rent and taxes; he sent the palace envoy back to the capital, and Emperor Suzong could not interrogate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He found bribes totaling several hundred thousand cash, reported them to the throne, and asked that the confiscated funds be applied to poor tenants' rent and taxes. He sent the supervising palace envoy back to the capital, and Suzong did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 肅宗親謁九宮神，慇勤於祠禱，皆玙所啟也。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong personally visited the Nine Palaces spirits and was earnest in temple prayers—all of this was initiated by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong's personal worship at the Nine Palaces shrines and his fervent ritual devotions were all Yu's doing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，罷知政事，為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was removed from handling state affairs and made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he left the chancellery and was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，兼揚州長史、御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan he was concurrently made Senior Administrator of Yangzhou and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 (761) he was also appointed Senior Administrator of Yangzhou and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 兗淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Concurrently Huainan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Huainan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 肅宗南郊禮畢，以玙使持節都督越州諸軍事、越州刺史，充浙江東道節度觀察處置使，本官兼御史大夫，祠祭使如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong completed the southern suburb rites, Yu was made Commissioner with credentials to supervise all military affairs of Yue Prefecture and Prefect of Yue, and Military Commissioner, Observation Commissioner, and Disposition Commissioner of Zhejiang East Circuit; his original offices of concurrent Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzong completed the southern suburban sacrifices, Yu was sent with credentials as overall commander of Yuezhou forces and as Prefect of Yue, and was made Military, Observation, and Disposition Commissioner for Zhejiang East Circuit, retaining his posts as Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner of Sacrificial Rites.

sentences.zh: 入為太子少保，轉少師。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and later promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 大曆三年六月卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Dali he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Dali 3 (768).

sentences.zh: 玙以祭祀妖妄致位將相，時以左道進者，往往有之。

translations.literal: Yu, through delusive sacrificial practices, attained the rank of general and chief minister; at the time those who advanced by heterodox ways were often to be found.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had risen to general and chief minister through superstitious ritualism, and many others at the time advanced by similar heterodox means.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年八月，道士李國禎以道術見，因奏皇室仙系，宜修崇靈跡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Guangde, the Daoist Li Guozhen was received for his Daoist arts, and memorialized that the imperial house's immortal lineage should have its numinous traces repaired and honored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Guangde 2 (764), the Daoist Li Guozhen gained audience through his occult arts and urged that the imperial clan's immortal lineage be honored by restoring its sacred sites.

sentences.zh: 請於昭應縣南三十里山頂置天華上宮露台、大地婆父、三皇、道君、太古天皇、中古伏羲媧皇等祠堂，並置掃灑宮戶一百戶。

translations.literal: He requested that on the mountaintop thirty li south of Zhaoying County be established the Heavenly Flower Upper Palace terrace, halls to the Great Earth Mother and Father, the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist Lord, the Most Ancient Celestial Emperor, the Middle Ancient Fuxi and Nüwa, and other shrines, and also one hundred households assigned as sweeping palace households.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that shrines be built on a mountaintop thirty li south of Zhaoying County—including the Heavenly Flower Upper Palace terrace, the Great Earth Mother and Father, the Three Sovereigns, the Daoist Lord, the Most Ancient Celestial Emperor, and Fuxi and Nüwa of middle antiquity—and that one hundred households be assigned to maintain them.

sentences.zh: 又於縣之東義扶谷故湫置龍堂，並許之。

translations.literal: He also requested establishing a Dragon Hall at the old pool in Yifu Valley east of the county, and all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed a Dragon Hall at the old pool in Yifu Valley east of the county, and the court approved both plans.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑荒，人甚不安，昭應縣令梁鎮上表曰：

translations.literal: At the time there was famine year after year and the people were greatly unsettled; the Magistrate of Zhaoying County, Liang Zhen, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Famine had gripped the land and the people were in distress. Magistrate Liang Zhen of Zhaoying County submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞國以人為本，害其本則非國；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the state takes the people as its foundation—if one harms the foundation, it is no longer a state;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state rests upon its people; harm the foundation and it ceases to be a state;

sentences.zh: 神以人為主，虐其主則非神。

translations.literal: spirits take the people as their masters—if one maltreats the masters, they are no longer spirits.
translations.idiomatic: and that spirits take the people as their masters; maltreat the masters and they are no longer worthy of worship.

sentences.zh: 故昔之聖王，所以極陳理道，明著祀典，將愛其人而慎用其財力，敬其神而虔恭於祠祭。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of old fully expounded the Way and principle, clearly set forth the sacrificial canon, intending to cherish their people and carefully use their wealth and labor, revere their spirits and be devout and reverent in sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of old therefore expounded the Way at length, defined the sacrificial canon clearly, cherished their people and husbanded their resources, and honored the spirits with sincere ritual devotion.

sentences.zh: 故神享其明德而降之福，人受其大賚而盡其力，然後神人以和，而國家可保也。

translations.literal: Thus the spirits enjoyed their bright virtue and bestowed blessings; the people received their great bounty and gave their full strength—only then were spirits and people in harmony and the state could be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Then the spirits accepted their bright virtue and sent down blessings, the people received royal bounty and gave their full effort, and only then could spirits and people live in harmony and the state endure.

sentences.zh: 一昨蟊賊作孽，水旱為災，雖王畿皆遍，而臣縣最苦。

translations.literal: Recently rebels have wrought havoc and flood and drought have become disasters; though the entire capital region has suffered, your subject's county has suffered most bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels have ravaged the land and flood and drought have struck; though the capital region has suffered everywhere, my county has borne the worst of it.

sentences.zh: 此則神之不能御大災明矣，又何力於陛下而得列祀典哉！

translations.literal: This makes clear that the spirits cannot ward off great disasters—what power do they have to aid Your Majesty that they should be entered in the sacrificial canon!
translations.idiomatic: This proves plainly that the spirits cannot avert great calamities. What power have they to aid Your Majesty that they deserve a place in the state cult?

sentences.zh: 用以殘弊之餘，當凶荒之歲，丁壯素出家入仕，羸老方飛芻輓粟，令但供億王事，已不堪命，更奔走鬼道，何以聊生？

translations.literal: To use what remains of the exhausted and ruined, in years of famine and disaster, when able-bodied men have long since left home for office and the frail elderly are just now hauling fodder and grain—now ordered only to supply the king's affairs, they already cannot bear the burden; to make them further rush about in ghostly ways—how can they sustain life?
translations.idiomatic: To demand more of a people already broken, in years of famine, when the able-bodied have long since left for government service and the aged barely manage to haul grain—men who can scarcely meet the crown's levies—how can they also be driven to serve these ghostly cults and still survive?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞天地之神，尊之極者，掃地可祭，精意可饗。

translations.literal: Your subject has further heard that for the spirits of Heaven and Earth, those most honored may be sacrificed to with swept ground, and with pure intent may be feasted.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the greatest spirits of Heaven and Earth may be worshipped with swept ground alone and received with pure sincerity.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦何必廢先王之典，崇俗巫之說，走南畝之客，殺東鄰之牛，而後冀非妄之福。

translations.literal: Why must Your Majesty abandon the canons of the former kings, exalt vulgar shaman teachings, drive off the guests of the southern fields, slaughter the eastern neighbor's ox, and only then hope for blessings that are not delusive?
translations.idiomatic: Why must Your Majesty abandon the rites of the ancient kings, exalt vulgar shamanism, drive farmers from their fields, slaughter the neighbor's ox, and only then hope for blessings that are not vain?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲為人祈福，福未至而人已困矣！

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty wishes to seek blessings for the people, before blessings arrive the people are already distressed!
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty wishes to bless the people, blessings have not arrived and the people are already exhausted!

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason the proposal must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 陛下不視昔者有道之君，至德之後，曷不卑宮室，惡飲食，恭己以遂萬物之性哉！

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty not look upon the rulers of old who possessed the Way, the heirs of utmost virtue—why do they not lower their palaces, abhor lavish food and drink, and with reverent self-restraint allow the nature of the myriad things to be fulfilled!
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty not consider the sage rulers of old, heirs of supreme virtue, who humbled their palaces, abhorred extravagance, and governed with reverent restraint so that all things might flourish?

sentences.zh: 陛下今違神亭育之心，竭人疲睏之力，如是又何從而致其福哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty now violates the spirits' heart of nurturing and sustaining, exhausts the people's weary and exhausted strength—how then can blessings be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now defies the nurturing spirit of Heaven and exhausts a people already worn down—how can blessings possibly follow?

sentences.zh: 此又不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 又陛下宗廟之敬極矣，尚無一月三祭之禮；

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty's reverence for the ancestral temple is already extreme, yet there is still no rite of three sacrifices in one month;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's devotion to the ancestral temple is already supreme, yet even there no rite calls for three sacrifices in a single month;

sentences.zh: 今此獨為，則宗廟之靈，將等以親疏，校以厚薄，陛下又何以言哉？

translations.literal: if this alone is done, then the spirits of the ancestral temple will be ranked by closeness and remoteness and measured by thick and thin—what can Your Majesty say to that?
translations.idiomatic: yet this cult alone would be singled out for lavish worship. How then can the ancestral spirits be ranked by kinship and measured by favor? What defense can Your Majesty offer?

sentences.zh: 此又不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 又大地婆父，祀典無文，言甚不經，義無可取。

translations.literal: Moreover the Great Earth Mother and Father have no textual basis in the sacrificial canon; the words are very unorthodox and the principle is not worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: The cult of the Great Earth Mother and Father has no place in the canonical rites; the doctrine is absurd and the principle worthless.

sentences.zh: 若陛下待與大地建祖宗之廟，必上天貽向背之責，陛下又何以為詞哉？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty intends to build an ancestral temple for the Great Earth alongside them, Heaven will surely impose the blame of favor and disfavor—what words can Your Majesty offer then?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty erects an ancestral temple to the Great Earth, Heaven itself will hold you accountable for reversing proper order. What answer will Your Majesty give?

sentences.zh: 此又不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 夫湫者，龍之所居也。

translations.literal: A pool is where dragons dwell.
translations.idiomatic: A sacred pool is the dragon's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 龍得水則神，無水則螻蟻之匹也。

translations.literal: When a dragon obtains water it is numinous; without water it is the equal of ants.
translations.idiomatic: A dragon with water is divine; without water it is no more than an ant.

sentences.zh: 故知水存則龍在，水竭則龍亡，此愚智之所同知矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when water remains the dragon is present, and when water is exhausted the dragon perishes—this is what fool and sage alike know.
translations.idiomatic: Where water remains, the dragon remains; where water fails, the dragon is gone—this fool and sage alike understand.

sentences.zh: 今湫竭已久，龍安所存？

translations.literal: Now the pool has long been dry—where can the dragon exist?
translations.idiomatic: The pool has been dry for years—where can any dragon abide?

sentences.zh: 陛下又崇飾祠宇，豐潔薦奠，為去龍之穴，破生人之產，人且怨矣，神何歆哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty further honors and adorns the shrine buildings and makes offerings rich and pure, thereby removing the dragon's lair and destroying the living people's livelihood—the people already resent it; how can the spirits delight in it!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty would lavishly adorn shrines and heap offerings at a site the dragon has abandoned, ruining the livelihood of the living. The people already resent it—what spirit could accept such worship?

sentences.zh: 此又不可五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 其道君、三皇、五帝，則兩京及所都之處，皆建宮觀祠廟，時設齋醮饗祀，國有彝典，官有常禮，蓋無闕失，何勞神役靈？

translations.literal: As for the Daoist Lord, the Three Sovereigns, and the Five Emperors, in both capitals and wherever the court resides, palace observatories and temples are all established, and fasting rituals and sacrificial feasts are regularly set—the state has constant statutes and officials have regular rites; there is basically no deficiency—why trouble spirits to compel numinous power?
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Lord, the Three Sovereigns, and the Five Emperors already have temples and observatories in both capitals and wherever the court resides, with regular fasts and sacrifices prescribed by statute. Nothing is lacking—why summon spirits to do the work again?

sentences.zh: 此又不可六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 臣稽先王之典禮，觀前聖之軌躅，休咎豐凶，災祥禍福，必主帝王五事，不在山川百神。

translations.literal: Your subject has examined the rituals of the former kings and observed the footprints of the earlier sages: fortune and misfortune, abundance and dearth, omens auspicious and calamitous, blessings and disasters—all must depend on the five affairs of the emperor, not on the hundred spirits of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I have studied the rites of the ancient kings and the example of the sages: fortune and misfortune, plenty and famine, omens good and ill—all depend on the sovereign's five duties, not on the myriad spirits of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 此又不可七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh reason it must be rejected.

sentences.zh: 臣伏察此弊，頗知其由。

translations.literal: Your subject, bowing low, has examined this abuse and knows its cause fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: I have looked closely into this abuse and understand its cause.

sentences.zh: 蓋以道士李國禎等動眾則得人，興工則獲利，祭祀則受胙，主執則弄權。

translations.literal: It is because Daoists such as Li Guozhen, when they mobilize the masses, gain followers; when they launch construction, obtain profit; when sacrifices are performed, receive sacrificial meat; when they hold charge, manipulate power.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists such as Li Guozhen gain followers by mobilizing crowds, profit from construction, receive sacrificial portions from rites, and wield power once put in charge.

sentences.zh: 是以鼓動禁中，熒惑天聽，踰越險阻，負荷粢盛，以日系年，無時而息。

translations.literal: Therefore they stir up the inner palace, dazzle the emperor's hearing, cross dangerous passes, bear grain offerings, day following day and year following year, without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they agitate within the palace, mislead the emperor's ear, cross dangerous terrain, and burden the people with grain levies—day after day, year after year, without pause.

sentences.zh: 曾不謂神功力，空止竭人膏血，以使人神胥怨，災孽並生。

translations.literal: They never consider the spirits' power; they merely exhaust the people's lifeblood, so that spirits and people alike resent, and disasters and calamities arise together.
translations.idiomatic: They never credit the spirits with any power; they only drain the people's lifeblood until spirits and men alike resent the court and disasters multiply.

sentences.zh: 罔上害人，左道亂政，原情定罪，非殺而何！

translations.literal: Deceiving the ruler and harming the people, heterodox ways disordering government—examining the circumstances and fixing guilt, if not execution then what!
translations.idiomatic: They deceive the throne, harm the people, and subvert government by heterodox means. Judged by their intent, what punishment but death is fitting?

sentences.zh: 臣昨受命之時，親承聖旨，務存安緝，許逐權宜。

translations.literal: When your subject yesterday received his commission, he personally received the sacred directive to strive to preserve peace and order, and was permitted to pursue expedients.
translations.idiomatic: When I took office I received Your Majesty's instruction to preserve peace and was authorized to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 誠願沉鄴縣之巫，安流弊之俗，其所興兩祠土木之功、丹青之役、三六之祭、灑掃之戶，謹明宣旨，並以權宜停訖。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish to sink the shamans of Ye County and settle the corrupt customs of the floating populace; the two shrines' earth-and-wood works, cinnabar-and-green labors, three-six sacrifices, and sweeping households—all have been clearly announced by imperial order and, by expedient authority, halted to completion.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly wish to suppress the shamans as Ye County did and restore a people abused by corrupt custom. By Your Majesty's order I have halted construction on both shrines, suspended painting work, stopped the thrice-daily sacrifices, and disbanded the maintenance households.

sentences.zh: 人吏百姓等，知陛下以從善為心，嫉惡為務，蠲除不急，劃革煩苛，皆喧呼於庭，抃躍於路，所徵糧糗，無不樂輸。

translations.literal: Officials, clerks, commoners, and others, knowing that Your Majesty takes following goodness as his heart and hating evil as his task, remitting what is not urgent and cutting away troublesome exactions, all shout in the courtyards and clap and leap in the roads; whatever grain and provisions are levied, none fail to pay gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike, seeing that Your Majesty welcomes good counsel and abhors evil, rejoice in court and dance in the streets at the removal of needless burdens. Whatever levies remain, they pay gladly.

sentences.zh: 臣伏以國禎等並交結中貴，狡蠹成性，臣雖忘身許國，不懼讒構，終恐賄及豪右，復為奸惡。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures that Guozhen and the others all associate with palace favorites; craft and corruption are their nature. Though your subject forgets his person in serving the state and does not fear slander, he ultimately fears that bribes will reach powerful families and they will again become wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen and his fellows consort with palace favorites and are corrupt by nature. Though I am ready to risk myself for the state and do not fear slander, I fear that once bribes reach the powerful they will resume their abuses.

sentences.zh: 其國禎等見據狀推勘，如獲贓狀，伏望許臣徵收，便充當縣郵館本用。

translations.literal: As for Guozhen and the others, judging from the evidence in the investigation it is as if stolen goods were obtained; your subject bows and hopes Your Majesty will permit him to collect and confiscate them, and immediately apply them to the county relay station's regular expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The evidence against Guozhen and his associates warrants confiscation as in a theft case. I beg leave to seize their property and apply it to the county relay station's operating costs.

sentences.zh: 其湫既竭，不可更置祠堂，又不當為大地建立祖廟，臣並請停。

translations.literal: The pool being already dry, no shrine may be further established, nor should an ancestral temple be built for the Great Earth—your subject requests that all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The pool is dry and no shrine should be built there; nor should an ancestral temple be raised to the Great Earth. I ask that both projects be halted.

sentences.zh: 其三皇、道君、天皇、伏羲、女媧等，既先各有宮廟，望請並於本所依禮齋祭。

translations.literal: The Three Sovereigns, Daoist Lord, Celestial Emperor, Fuxi, Nüwa, and the like already each have palace temples elsewhere; your subject hopes they may all be worshipped with fasting sacrifices at their original sites according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns, Daoist Lord, Celestial Emperor, Fuxi, Nüwa, and the rest already have temples elsewhere. I ask that they be worshipped only at those established sites according to proper rite.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 李泌，字長源，其先遼東襄平人，西魏太保、八柱國司徒徒何弼之六代孫。

translations.literal: Li Bi, style name Changyuan, his ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong, sixth-generation descendant of Tuohe Bi, Grand Guardian and one of the Eight Pillars, Minister of Education of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, courtesy name Changyuan, was descended from Xiangping in Liaodong—six generations removed from Tuohe Bi, Grand Guardian and Minister of Education, one of the Eight Pillars of Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 今居京兆吳房令承休之子。

translations.literal: Now residing in Jingzhao, son of Wu Fang Magistrate Chengxiu.
translations.idiomatic: His family now lived in the capital region; he was the son of Magistrate Chengxiu of Wufang.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，博涉經史，精究《易象》，善屬文，尤工於詩，以王佐自負。

translations.literal: From youth clever and keen, he broadly traversed the classics and histories, thoroughly investigated the Images of the Changes, was skilled at literary composition, especially accomplished in poetry, and prided himself on being a king's assistant.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was brilliant, widely read in the classics and histories, and deeply versed in the Book of Changes. He wrote well and excelled especially at poetry, holding himself capable of ministering to a sage ruler.

sentences.zh: 張九齡、韋虛心、張廷珪皆器重之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, Wei Xuxin, and Zhang Tinggui all greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, Wei Xuxin, and Zhang Tinggui all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 泌操尚不羈，恥隨常格仕進。

translations.literal: Bi's conduct and aims were unrestrained; he was ashamed to follow the usual paths to office and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's temperament was free-spirited, and he disdained the conventional path to office.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，自嵩山上書論當世務，玄宗召見，令侍詔翰林，仍東宮供奉。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, from Mount Song he submitted a memorial discussing affairs of the age; Emperor Xuanzong summoned him for audience, ordered him to attend as Hanlin Drafting Attendant, and also to serve the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he sent a memorial from Mount Song on affairs of state. Xuanzong summoned him, appointed him Hanlin attendant, and assigned him to the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠忌其才辯，奏泌嘗為《感遇詩》，諷刺時政，詔於蘄春郡安置，乃潛遁名山，以習隱自適。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong resented his talent and eloquence, and memorialized that Bi had once written "Poems on Encountering Fate," satirizing current policy; an edict ordered him settled in Qichun Prefecture, whereupon he secretly fled to famous mountains and took to practicing reclusion for his own ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, jealous of his brilliance, accused him of satirizing the government in his "Poems on Encountering Fate." An edict banished him to Qichun, but Bi fled into the mountains and lived as a recluse.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，祿山構難，肅宗北巡，至靈武即位，遣使訪召。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Lushan raised rebellion; Emperor Suzong toured north, ascended the throne at Lingwu, and dispatched envoys to seek and summon him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, An Lushan rebelled. Suzong marched north, took the throne at Lingwu, and sent envoys to find him.

sentences.zh: 會泌自嵩、潁間冒難奔赴行在，至彭原郡謁見，陳古今成敗之機，甚稱旨，延致臥內，動皆顧問。

translations.literal: It happened that Bi from between Song and Ying braved hardship and rushed to the mobile court; arriving at Pengyuan Prefecture he had audience, expounded the mechanisms of success and failure in ancient and modern times, greatly pleased the emperor, was received within the sleeping quarters, and in every movement was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Bi himself hurried from the Song and Ying region through the turmoil to the mobile court. At Pengyuan he had audience, expounded the patterns of rise and fall through history, and greatly pleased the emperor, who kept him at his bedside and consulted him on every matter.

sentences.zh: 泌稱山人，固辭官秩，特以散官寵之，解褐拜銀青光祿大夫，俾掌樞務。

translations.literal: Bi styled himself a mountain man and firmly declined official rank; he was specially favored with a sinecure office, and upon leaving the cloth was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and made to manage pivotal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi called himself a mountain recluse and refused regular office, but the emperor honored him with a sinecure title, appointing him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and entrusting him with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 至於四言文狀、將相遷除，皆與泌參議，權逾宰相，仍判元帥廣平王軍司馬事。

translations.literal: As for four-character documents and memorials, and the transfer and dismissal of generals and ministers—all were deliberated with Bi; his authority exceeded the chief minister's, and he still concurrently served as Army Vice Marshal on the staff of the Marshal Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials in four-character prose and appointments of generals and ministers were all discussed with Bi. His authority exceeded that of the chief minister, and he also served as army vice marshal on the staff of the Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 肅宗每謂曰：「卿當上皇天寶中，為朕師友，下判廣平行軍，朕父子三人，資卿道義。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong often said to him: "You, sir, in the Tianbao era under the Retired Emperor, were teacher and friend to me; below you direct the Guangping prince's army—we father and son three men rely on your Way and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong often told him, "In the Tianbao years under the Retired Emperor you were teacher and friend to me; now you direct the Prince of Guangping's army. We three—father and sons—depend on your counsel and integrity."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he valued.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 尋為中書令崔圓、幸臣李輔國害其能，將有不利於泌。

translations.literal: Before long Chief Minister Cui Yuan and the favored minister Li Fuguo, resenting his ability, were about to act to Bi's detriment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chief Minister Cui Yuan and the favorite Li Fuguo, jealous of his talent, plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 泌懼，乞游衡山，優詔許之，給以三品祿俸，遂隱衡岳，絕粒棲神。

translations.literal: Bi feared this and requested to wander Mount Heng; a gracious edict permitted it and granted third-rank salary; he then hid on Mount Heng, abstained from grain, and dwelt in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Bi asked leave to retire to Mount Heng. A gracious edict granted his request with third-rank stipend, and he lived in seclusion on the sacred mountain, fasting and cultivating the spirit.

sentences.zh: 興元初，征赴行在，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was summoned to the mobile court and promoted to Left Regular Attendant of the Palace Riding.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xingyuan reign he was summoned to court and promoted to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，除陝州長史，充陝、虢都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was made Senior Administrator of Shan Prefecture and Military Commissioner of the Shan-Guo Metropolitan Defense and Observation Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 (785) he was appointed Senior Administrator of Shanzhou and Military Commissioner of the Shan-Guo defense circuit.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，泌奏：「虢州盧氏山冶，近出瑟瑟，請充獻，禁人開採。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, Bi memorialized: "The smelting works at Mount Lushi in Guo Prefecture have recently produced sese gems; your subject requests they be offered in tribute and that people be forbidden to mine them."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year Bi memorialized: "The smeltery at Mount Lushi in Guozhou has lately yielded sese gems. I ask that they be reserved for tribute and that private mining be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「瑟瑟之寶，中土所無今產於近甸，實為靈貺。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The treasure of sese— the central land did not have it; now produced in the nearby fields, it is truly a numinous gift."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Sese gems are unknown in the central plains; that they now appear in our own domain is indeed a divine gift."

sentences.zh: 朕不飾器玩，不尚珍奇，常思返朴之風，用明躬儉之節。

translations.literal: We do not adorn vessels and playthings, do not esteem rare curiosities, constantly think of returning to simplicity's wind, and use this to manifest personal frugality's measure.
translations.idiomatic: We do not adorn ourselves with luxuries or prize rare curios; we ever seek the spirit of simplicity and practice personal frugality."

sentences.zh: 其出瑟瑟之處，任百姓求采，不宜禁止。

translations.literal: Where sese is produced, let the common people seek and gather it; it should not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Let the people mine sese where it is found; it should not be prohibited."

sentences.zh: 」就加泌檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally made Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was thereupon additionally appointed Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時陳、許戍邊卒三千自京西逃歸，至州境，泌潛師險隘，左右攻擊，盡誅之。

translations.literal: At the time three thousand border garrison soldiers of Chen and Xu who had fled from west of the capital returned to their home region; reaching the prefectural border, Bi secretly deployed troops in narrow passes and attacked from both sides, executing them all.
translations.idiomatic: When three thousand Chen and Xu border troops deserted from west of the capital and entered his jurisdiction, Bi ambushed them in a narrow pass and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 尋拜中書侍郎、平章事、集賢崇文館學士、修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Minister, Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies and Hall for Venerating Culture, and Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Minister, Academician of the imperial libraries, and Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 初，張延賞大減官員，人情咨怨，泌請復之，以從人欲，因是奏罷兼試額內佔闕等官，加百官俸料，隨閒劇加置手力課，上從之，人人以為便。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Yanshang had greatly reduced official posts, and popular sentiment murmured in resentment; Bi requested restoring them to follow people's desires, and thereby memorialized to abolish officials who occupied vacancies within the combined examination quota, increased all officials' salary provisions, and added hand-labor levies according to whether duties were light or heavy; the emperor followed this, and everyone considered it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Yanshang had drastically cut the bureaucracy, provoking widespread resentment. Bi proposed restoring posts to satisfy public opinion, abolishing officials who held supernumerary slots, raising salaries, and adding clerical allowances scaled to each post's workload. The emperor approved, and all regarded the reforms as beneficial.

sentences.zh: 而竇參旁奏，遂改易，使同品之內，月俸多少累等。

translations.literal: But Dou Can submitted a side memorial, and it was then altered so that within the same rank monthly salaries had many gradations.
translations.idiomatic: But Dou Can intervened with a side memorial, and the plan was altered so that officials of the same rank received widely differing monthly salaries.

sentences.zh: 泌又奏請罷拾遺、補闕，上雖不從，亦不授人，故諫司惟韓皋、歸登而已。

translations.literal: Bi again memorialized requesting abolition of the Reminder and Supplementation posts; although the emperor did not agree, he also did not appoint anyone, so the Remonstrance Bureau had only Han Gao and Gui Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi again asked to abolish the Reminder and Supplementation posts. The emperor refused, but he also appointed no one else, so the Remonstrance Bureau held only Han Gao and Gui Deng.

sentences.zh: 泌仍命收其署湌錢，令登等寓食於中書舍人，故時戲云：「韓諫議雖分左右，歸拾遺莫辨存亡。

translations.literal: Bi still ordered collection of their office meal money and had Deng and the others lodge and eat with the Central Secretariat drafters, hence the jest of the time: "Though Han the Remonstrator divides left and right, for Gui the Reminder one cannot tell alive from dead."
translations.idiomatic: Bi still confiscated their office meal allowances and made Deng and the others board and eat with the Secretariat drafters, whence the jest: "Han the Remonstrator may divide left from right, but for Gui the Reminder you cannot tell the living from the dead."

sentences.zh: 」如是者三年。

translations.literal: Thus it went on for three years.
translations.idiomatic: This continued for three years.

sentences.zh: 至貞元五年，以前東都防禦判官、殿中侍御史、內供奉韋綬為左補闕，監察御史梁肅右補闕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, the former Eastern Capital defense staff judge, Palace Attendant censor, and inner attendant Wei Shou was made Left Supplementation, and the Investigating Censor Liang Su Right Supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Wei Shou—former staff judge of the Eastern Capital defense command, Palace Attendant censor, and inner attendant—was appointed Left Supplementation, and Investigating Censor Liang Su was appointed Right Supplementation.

sentences.zh: 既復置，人心忻然。

translations.literal: Once the posts were restored, people's hearts rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Once the offices were restored, public sentiment brightened.

sentences.zh: 順宗在春宮，妃蕭氏母郜國公主交通外人，上疑其有他，連坐貶黜者數人，皇儲亦危。

translations.literal: Shunzong was in the Eastern Palace; his consort the Xiao clan's mother, Princess Gouguo, had improper dealings with outsiders; the emperor suspected other matters; several were punished by association; the heir apparent was also endangered.
translations.idiomatic: While Shunzong was heir apparent, the mother of his consort of the Xiao clan—Princess Gouguo—was found to have improper dealings with outsiders. The emperor suspected worse, several people were punished by association, and the crown prince himself was imperiled.

sentences.zh: 泌百端奏說，上意方解。

translations.literal: Bi pleaded by every means in memorials, and only then did the emperor's mind ease.
translations.idiomatic: Bi argued the matter from every angle in memorials, and the emperor's suspicions were finally allayed.

sentences.zh: 泌頗有讜直之風，而談神仙詭道，或云嘗與赤松子、王喬、安期、羨門游處，故為代所輕，雖詭道求容，不為時君所重。

translations.literal: Bi had quite a forthright remonstrance style, yet spoke of immortals and strange ways; some said he had once kept company with Chisongzi, Wang Qiao, Anqi, and Xianmen, and so his age slighted him; though he used strange ways to win favor, the sovereigns of the time did not value him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had a reputation for blunt remonstrance, yet he also spoke of immortals and occult arts; rumor held that he had once consorted with Chisongzi, Wang Qiao, Anqi, and Xianmen. His contemporaries therefore looked down on him, and although he courted favor through esoteric talk, the rulers of his day did not truly esteem him.

sentences.zh: 德宗初即位，尤惡巫祝怪誕之士。

translations.literal: When Dezong first took the throne, he especially hated shamans, sacrificial diviners, and bizarre eccentric scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first ascended the throne, he especially detested shamans, temple diviners, and bizarre occultists.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗重陰陽祠祝之說，用妖人王玙為宰相，或命巫媼乘驛行郡縣以為厭勝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Suzong valued the doctrines of yin-yang and sacrificial divination, employed the sorcerer Wang Yu as chief minister, and sometimes ordered witch crones to travel by post relay through prefectures and counties for exorcistic victory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Suzong had favored yin-yang lore and temple divination, appointed the sorcerer Wang Yu as chief minister, and sometimes sent witch-women by courier post through the prefectures and counties to perform exorcistic rites.

sentences.zh: 凡有所興造功役，動牽禁忌。

translations.literal: Whenever any construction or labor project was undertaken, it was constantly entangled in taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Every construction project or public work was hemmed in by taboos.

sentences.zh: 而黎干用左道位至尹京，嘗內集眾工，編刺珠繡為御衣，既成而焚之，以為禳禬，且無虛月。

translations.literal: Li Qian, by left-hand ways, rose to magistrate of the capital; he once gathered artisans within, wove and embroidered pearls into imperial robes, and when they were finished burned them as expiation rites—not a month went by without it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian rose to capital magistrate through heterodox practices; he once assembled artisans inside the palace to weave pearl-embroidered imperial robes, then burned them upon completion as expiatory rites—hardly a month passed without such a ceremony.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮，頗知其事，即位之後，罷集僧於內道場，除巫祝之祀。

translations.literal: Dezong, while in the Eastern Palace, knew these matters well; after he took the throne he abolished gathering monks at the inner dharma altar and removed shaman sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had learned of these practices as crown prince; once enthroned he stopped assembling monks at the inner chapel and abolished shaman rites.

sentences.zh: 有司言宣政內廊壞，請修繕。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported that the inner corridor of Xuanzheng Hall was damaged and requested repairs.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported damage to the inner corridor of Xuanzheng Hall and asked permission to repair it.

sentences.zh: 而太卜云：「孟冬為魁岡，不利穿築，請卜他月。

translations.literal: But the Grand Diviner said: "Midwinter is the Kui Ridge—unfavorable for digging and building; please divine another month."
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand Diviner said, "Midwinter falls under the Kui Ridge taboo and is unfavorable for excavation; please choose another month by divination."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「《春秋》之義，啟塞從時，何魁岡之有？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that opening and closing follow the season—what Kui Ridge is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that work should follow the seasons—what Kui Ridge taboo is there?"

sentences.zh: 」卒命修之。

translations.literal: He finally ordered repairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the repairs carried out.

sentences.zh: 又代宗山陵靈駕發引，上號送於承天門，見辒辌不當道，稍指午未間。

translations.literal: Again, when the spiritual carriage for Daizong's imperial tomb set out, the emperor wailed in escort at Chengtian Gate and saw the hearse not in the proper route, angled slightly toward the noon and wei hours.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when the imperial catafalque for Daizong's tomb departed, the emperor wailed in farewell at Chengtian Gate and noticed the hearse routed off the main way, angled slightly toward the noon and wei directions.

sentences.zh: 問其故，有司對曰：「陛下本命在午，故不敢當道。

translations.literal: He asked the reason; the offices replied: "Your Majesty's natal destiny lies in the Wu hour, so we dared not block the route."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, the officials answered, "Your Majesty's natal destiny lies in the Wu hour, so we dared not place the hearse in your path."

sentences.zh: 」上號泣曰：「安有枉靈駕而謀身利。

translations.literal: The emperor wailed and said: "How can there be bending the spiritual carriage to seek personal advantage?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sobbed, "How could one divert the imperial catafalque for one's own benefit?"

sentences.zh: 」卒命直午而行。

translations.literal: He finally ordered it to proceed straight through the noon route.
translations.idiomatic: He finally ordered the procession to pass straight along the noon meridian.

sentences.zh: 及建中末，寇戎內梗，桑道茂有城奉天之說，上稍以時日禁忌為意，而雅聞泌長於鬼道，故自外征還，以至大用，時論不以為愜。

translations.literal: By the end of Jianzhong, border raiders troubled the interior; Sang Daomao had a theory of fortifying Fengtian; the emperor grew somewhat mindful of day-and-month taboos and had long heard that Bi excelled at ghost ways, so he was summoned back from outside to great employment—contemporary opinion was not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Jianzhong era, rebels pressed inward; Sang Daomao urged fortifying Fengtian; the emperor grew mindful of calendrical taboos and had long heard that Li Bi was skilled in occult arts, so he recalled him from exile to high office—an appointment public opinion did not welcome.

sentences.zh: 及在相位，隨時俯仰，無足可稱。

translations.literal: Once in the chief minister's position, he bent with the times—nothing worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: In office as chief minister he simply bent with circumstances—nothing worth commending.

sentences.zh: 復引顧況輩輕薄之流，動為朝士戲侮，頗貽譏誚。

translations.literal: He again drew Gu Kuang and similar frivolous sorts, who were constantly mocked by court scholars and brought considerable ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: He again surrounded himself with Gu Kuang and other frivolous men, who were constantly mocked by the court and brought him much ridicule.

sentences.zh: 年六十八薨，贈太子太傅，賻禮有加。

translations.literal: At age sixty-eight he died; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with enhanced funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with unusually generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 泌放曠敏辯，好大言，自出入中禁，累為權幸忌嫉恆由智免；

translations.literal: Bi was unconstrained, keen, and eloquent, loved grand talk; since entering and leaving the inner palace he was repeatedly envied by powerful favorites but always escaped through wit;
translations.idiomatic: Bi was free-spirited, quick-witted, and fond of bold pronouncements; from the time he moved in and out of the inner palace, powerful favorites repeatedly envied him, yet he always escaped harm through his wits;

sentences.zh: 終以言論縱橫，上悟聖主，以躋相位。

translations.literal: in the end, through sweeping discourse he awakened the sage sovereign and ascended to the chief minister's post.
translations.idiomatic: and in the end, through forceful counsel he won over the sage emperor and rose to the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十捲。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子繁，少聰警，有才名，無行義。

translations.literal: His son Fan was clever and alert from youth, had a reputation for talent, but lacked moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan was bright from youth and won a name for talent, but he lacked moral character.

sentences.zh: 泌為相，嘗引薦夏縣處士北平陽城為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Bi was chief minister, he once recommended the Xi County recluse Yang Cheng of Beiping as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as chief minister, Bi once recommended Yang Cheng, a recluse of Xi County in Beiping, as Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 城道直，既遇知己，深德之。

translations.literal: Cheng's way was upright; having met a confidant, he was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was a man of integrity; having found a patron who understood him, he was deeply obliged.

sentences.zh: 及泌歿，戶部尚書裴延齡巧佞奉上，德宗信任，竊弄威權，舉朝側目。

translations.literal: When Bi died, the Minister of Revenue Pei Yanling, clever and fawning toward the sovereign, won Dezong's trust, secretly wielded authority, and the whole court glared sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: After Bi's death, Pei Yanling of the Ministry of Revenue—a sycophant who flattered the throne—won Dezong's trust and secretly wielded power while the whole court watched in alarm.

sentences.zh: 城中正之士，尤忿嫉之。

translations.literal: The upright men of the capital especially hated and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The upright men of the capital especially detested him.

sentences.zh: 一日盡疏其過惡，欲密論奏，以繁故人子，為可親信，遂示其疏草，兼請繁繕寫。

translations.literal: One day Cheng fully listed Yanling's faults and crimes and wished to present a secret memorial; because Fan was an old friend's son and deemed trustworthy, he showed him the draft and also asked Fan to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: One day Yang Cheng drafted a full catalogue of Yanling's crimes for a secret memorial. Trusting Fan as an old friend's son, he showed him the draft and asked him to make a fair copy.

sentences.zh: 繁既寫，悉能記之，其夕乃徑詣延齡，具述其事。

translations.literal: Once Fan had copied it, he could remember it all; that very evening he went straight to Yanling and told him everything in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Fan copied the text and memorized every word; that same evening he went straight to Yanling and disclosed the entire plan.

sentences.zh: 延齡聞之，即時請對，盡以城章中欲論事件，一一先自解。

translations.literal: Yanling, hearing of it, immediately requested audience and preemptively explained, one by one, every matter Cheng's memorial meant to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Yanling immediately sought an audience and preemptively answered every charge Cheng intended to raise.

sentences.zh: 及城疏入，德宗以為妄，不之省。

translations.literal: When Cheng's memorial entered, Dezong thought it false and did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng's memorial arrived, Dezong dismissed it as slander and paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 泌與右補闕、翰林學士梁肅友善，嘗命繁持所著文請肅潤色。

translations.literal: Bi and the Right Supplementation and Hanlin academician Liang Su were friendly; he once ordered Fan to bring his writings for Su to polish.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was on friendly terms with Liang Su, Right Supplementation and Hanlin academician, and once had Fan bring his writings to Su for revision.

sentences.zh: 繁亦自有學術，肅待之甚厚，因許師事，日熟其門。

translations.literal: Fan also had learning of his own; Su treated him very generously and permitted him to study as a disciple, daily growing familiar at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had learning of his own; Su treated him generously, accepted him as a disciple, and Fan frequented his household daily.

sentences.zh: 及肅卒，繁亂其配，士君子無不嘆駭，積年委棄。

translations.literal: When Su died, Fan molested his widow; gentlemen were all shocked and sighing, and for years he was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: After Su's death, Fan molested his widow. Men of honor were appalled, and for years he was shunned.

sentences.zh: 後起為太常博士，太常卿權德輿奏斥之，除河南府士曹掾。

translations.literal: Later he was raised as a doctorate of the Imperial Sacrifices; the Director Quan Deyu memorialized to expel him, and he was appointed clerical aide of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed a doctorate of the Imperial Sacrifices, but Director Quan Deyu memorialized for his removal and he was demoted to clerical aide in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以其警悟異常，泌之故人為宰相，左右援拯，後得累居郡守，而力學不倦。

translations.literal: Because he was extraordinarily alert and perceptive, and Bi's old friends served as chief ministers, they aided him on both sides; he later repeatedly held prefectural posts and studied tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his unusual brilliance and because Bi's old friends now held high office, patrons rescued him; he later served repeatedly as prefect and never ceased his studies.

sentences.zh: 罷隨州刺史，歸京師，久不承恩。

translations.literal: Dismissed from the prefecture of Suizhou, he returned to the capital and long received no imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the prefecture of Suizhou he returned to the capital but for a long time received no favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 韋處厚入相，厚待之。

translations.literal: When Wei Chuhou entered as chief minister, he treated Fan generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chuhou became chief minister, he treated Fan with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年六月，敬宗降誕日，御三殿，特詔兵部侍郎丁公著、太常少卿陸旦與繁等三人抗浮圖道士講論。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Baoli, on Jingzong's birthday commemoration, he held court in the Three Halls and specially ordered the Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu, the Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Dan, and Fan and two others to debate Buddhist monks and Daoist priests.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Baoli 2, on the commemoration of Jingzong's birth, the emperor held court in the Three Halls and specially ordered Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu, Vice Director of Sacrifices Lu Dan, Fan, and one other to debate Buddhist and Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 九月，除大理少卿，復加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and again made an academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and again made a Hongwen academician.

sentences.zh: 時諫官御史章疏相繼，宰臣不得已，出為亳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time remonstrators and censors submitted memorial after memorial; the chief ministers had no choice and sent him out as prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators and censors then submitted one memorial after another; the chief ministers had no choice but to appoint him prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州境嘗有群賊，剽人廬舍，劫取貨財，累政擒捕不獲。

translations.literal: The prefecture had bandit gangs that raided dwellings and plundered goods; successive administrations could not capture them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long suffered bandit gangs that raided homes and plundered property, and successive administrations had failed to capture them.

sentences.zh: 繁潛設機謀，悉知賊之巢穴，出兵盡加誅斬。

translations.literal: Fan secretly devised stratagems, knew all the bandits' lairs, deployed troops, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fan secretly laid plans, located every bandit nest, sent out troops, and executed the entire gang.

sentences.zh: 時議責繁以不先啟聞廉使，涉於擅興之罪，朝廷遣監察御史舒元輿按問。

translations.literal: Public opinion blamed Fan for not first informing the surveillance commissioner, bordering on the crime of unauthorized military action; the court sent the Investigating Censor Shu Yuanyu to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that Fan had failed to notify the surveillance commissioner beforehand and had thereby committed unauthorized military action; the court sent Investigating Censor Shu Yuanyu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 元輿素與繁有隙，復以初官，銳於生事，乃盡反其獄辭，以為繁濫殺無辜，狀奏，敕於京兆府賜死，時人冤之。

translations.literal: Yuanyu had long borne a grudge against Fan and, as a newcomer eager to make cases, completely reversed the testimony, claiming Fan had wantonly killed innocents; he memorialized, and an edict ordered execution by the capital prefecture—contemporaries thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu had long hated Fan and, eager to make his mark in a new post, reversed the entire case and accused Fan of slaughtering innocents. His memorial led to an edict ordering execution in the capital; contemporaries considered it a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 其後元輿被禍，人以為有報應焉。

translations.literal: Later Yuanyu met with disaster, and people regarded it as karmic retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanyu himself met with disaster, and people took it as retribution.

sentences.zh: 初，泌流放江南，與柳渾、顧況為人外之交，吟詠自適。

translations.literal: At first, when Bi was exiled to the south, he formed friendships beyond the ordinary with Liu Hun and Gu Kuang and chanted poetry for his own ease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Bi was exiled to the south, he formed an extraordinary friendship with Liu Hun and Gu Kuang and composed poetry for his own solace.

sentences.zh: 而渾先達，故泌復得入官於朝。

translations.literal: Liu Hun rose first, and so Bi was again able to enter office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun rose to office first, which enabled Bi to return to court.

sentences.zh: 顧況者，蘇州人。

translations.literal: Gu Kuang was a native of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Kuang was a native of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 能為歌詩，性詼諧，雖王公之貴與之交者，必戲侮之，然以嘲誚能文，人多狎之。

translations.literal: He could compose songs and poetry; his nature was humorous; even when nobles and dukes associated with him he had to mock them, yet because his satirical wit and literary skill were strong, many were familiar with him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote songs and poetry and had a humorous nature; even when dealing with nobles he mocked them, yet because his satire was sharp and his writing skilled, many courted his company.

sentences.zh: 柳渾輔政，以校書郎征。

translations.literal: When Liu Hun assisted in government, he was summoned as proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hun entered the government, Kuang was summoned as proofreader.

sentences.zh: 復遇李泌繼入，自謂己知秉樞要。

translations.literal: He again met Li Bi entering afterward and thought himself sure to wield the pivot of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bi followed him into office, Kuang assumed he would soon hold the levers of power.

sentences.zh: 當得達官，久之方遷著作郎。

translations.literal: He ought to have obtained a high office, but only after a long time was he promoted to Composition Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He expected a high post, yet only after a long delay was he promoted to Composition Officer.

sentences.zh: 況心不樂，求歸於吳。

translations.literal: Kuang's heart was not pleased, and he requested return to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Discontented, Kuang asked to return to Wu.

sentences.zh: 而班列群官，咸有侮玩之目，皆惡嫉之。

translations.literal: Yet among the ranked officials of the court all had eyes of mockery and play, and all hated and envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his colleagues in court ranks all looked on him with contempt, and everyone resented him.

sentences.zh: 及泌卒，不哭，而有調笑之言，為憲司所劾，貶饒州司戶。

translations.literal: When Bi died he did not mourn but uttered words of ridicule; the discipline office censured him and he was demoted to revenue clerk of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi died he did not mourn but made mocking remarks; the censorate impeached him and he was demoted to revenue clerk in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十捲。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 其《贈柳宜城》辭句，率多戲劇，文體皆此類也。

translations.literal: His "Presented to Liu of Yicheng"—its phrases were mostly playful drama, and his literary style was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His "Presented to Liu of Yicheng" is mostly playful burlesque; his writings are generally of that kind.

sentences.zh: 子非熊，登進士第，累佐使府，亦有詩名於時。

translations.literal: His son Feixiong passed the jinshi examination, repeatedly served on commissioner staffs, and also had a poetry reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feixiong passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly on military commissioners' staffs, and also won a name for poetry.

sentences.zh: 崔造，字玄宰，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Zao, courtesy name Xuanzai, was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zao, courtesy name Xuanzai, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 少涉學，永泰中，與韓會、盧東美、張正則為友，皆僑居上元，好談經濟之略，嘗以王佐自許，時人號為「四夔」。

translations.literal: In youth he studied broadly; in the Yongtai era he befriended Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze; all sojourned in Shangyuan, loved discussing statecraft, once prided themselves on being king's assistants, and contemporaries called them the "Four Kui."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied widely. In the Yongtai era he befriended Han Hui, Lu Dongmei, and Zhang Zhengze; all lived in Shangyuan, loved to discuss statecraft, styled themselves king's assistants, and were known as the "Four Kui."

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠引為賓僚，累至左司員外郎。

translations.literal: The Zhexi observation commissioner Li Qiyun recruited him as staff; he rose to Left Department vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun, observation commissioner of Zhexi, took him onto his staff, and he rose to vice director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 與劉晏善，及晏遭楊炎、庾准誣奏伏誅，造累貶信州長史。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Liu Yan; when Yan was slandered by Yang Yan and Yu Zhun and executed, Zao was repeatedly demoted to long history of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was friendly with Liu Yan; when Yan was framed by Yang Yan and Yu Zhun and executed, Zao was repeatedly demoted, ending as long history of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之逆，造為建州刺史，聞難作，馳檄鄰州，請齊舉義兵，遂調發所部，得二千人，德宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: At Zhu Ci's rebellion, Zao was prefect of Jianzhou; hearing trouble had arisen, he dispatched urgent proclamations to neighboring prefectures requesting that all raise righteous troops together; he mustered his district and obtained two thousand men; Dezong heard and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Zao was prefect of Jianzhou. Hearing of the uprising, he sent urgent proclamations to neighboring prefectures urging a joint loyalist levy, mustered two thousand men from his command, and Dezong praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 及收京師，詔征造至藍田，以舅源休明逆伏誅，上疏請罪，不敢即赴闕。

translations.literal: When the capital was recovered, an edict summoned Zao to Lantian; because his maternal uncle Yuan Xiu had clearly joined the rebellion and was executed, he submitted a memorial requesting punishment and dared not immediately come to court.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was retaken, an edict summoned him to Lantian. Because his uncle Yuan Xiu had openly joined the rebellion and been executed, Zao submitted a memorial asking to be punished and did not dare proceed immediately to court.

sentences.zh: 上以為知禮，優詔慰勉，拜吏部郎中、給事中。

translations.literal: The emperor thought he knew propriety, issued a gracious edict to comfort and encourage him, and appointed him director of the Bureau of Appointments and Presentation Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged him observant of propriety, sent a gracious edict of reassurance, and appointed him director of the Bureau of Appointments and Presentation Attendant.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年正月，與中書舍人齊映各守本官，同平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, he and the Central Secretariat drafter Qi Ying each kept their original posts and served together as Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenyuan 2 he and Central Secretariat drafter Qi Ying retained their original posts and were jointly appointed Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 時京畿兵亂之後，仍歲蝗旱，府無儲積。

translations.literal: At the time, after military turmoil in the capital region and successive years of locusts and drought, the treasury had no stores.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region had just endured military disorder, followed by successive locust plagues and drought; the government granaries stood empty.

sentences.zh: 德宗以造敢言，為能立事，故不次登用。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Zao dared speak and was able to accomplish affairs, therefore promoted him out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zao spoke boldly and seemed able to act decisively, Dezong promoted him out of turn.

sentences.zh: 造久從事江外，嫉錢谷諸使罔上之弊，乃奏天下兩稅錢物，委本道觀察使、本州刺史選官典部送上都；

translations.literal: Zao had long served south of the Yangzi and resented how the grain-and-money commissioners deceived the throne; he memorialized that the empire's two-tax money and goods should be entrusted to each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect to select officials to oversee delivery to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Having long served in the south, Zao resented the grain commissioners' habit of deceiving the throne. He proposed that all two-tax revenues be delivered under officials chosen by each circuit's observation commissioner and prefect;

sentences.zh: 諸道水陸運使及度支、巡院、江淮轉運使等並停；

translations.literal: all circuit water-and-land transport commissioners, the Revenue Bureau, inspection offices, and the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner were to be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: and that circuit transport commissioners, the Revenue Bureau's inspection offices, and the Jiang-Huai transport commissioner be abolished;

sentences.zh: 其度支、鹽鐵，委尚書省本司判；

translations.literal: revenue and salt-iron affairs were to be adjudicated by the responsible departments of the Ministry of State;
translations.idiomatic: while revenue and salt-iron affairs were to be handled by the appropriate bureaus of the Ministry of State;

sentences.zh: 其尚書省六職，令宰臣分判。

translations.literal: and the six duties of the Ministry of State were to be divided among the chief ministers for adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: and the six ministries were to be divided among the chief ministers for supervision.

sentences.zh: 乃以戶部侍郎元琇判諸道鹽鐵、榷酒等事；

translations.literal: Then the Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu was assigned to adjudicate all circuits' salt-iron and monopoly wine affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiu was assigned salt-iron and wine monopolies across all circuits;

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎吉中孚判度支及諸道兩稅事；

translations.literal: the Vice Minister of Revenue Ji Zhongfu was assigned the Revenue Bureau and all circuits' two-tax affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Ji Zhongfu was assigned the Revenue Bureau and the two-tax system;

sentences.zh: 宰臣齊映判兵部承旨及雜事；

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Qi Ying was assigned the War Ministry drafting and miscellaneous affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Qi Ying took the War Ministry and miscellaneous drafting;

sentences.zh: 宰臣李勉判刑部；

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Li Mian was assigned the Punishments Ministry;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Li Mian took the Punishments Ministry;

sentences.zh: 宰臣劉滋判吏部、禮部；

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Liu Zi was assigned the Appointments and Rites ministries;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Liu Zi took Appointments and Rites;

sentences.zh: 造判戶部、工部。

translations.literal: and Zao was assigned the Revenue and Works ministries.
translations.idiomatic: and Zao took Revenue and Works.

sentences.zh: 又以歲飢，浙江東西道入運米每年七十五萬石，今更令兩稅折納米一百萬石，委兩浙節度使韓滉運送一百萬石至東渭橋；

translations.literal: Also, because it was a famine year, the east and west circuits of Zhejiang had previously sent seven hundred fifty thousand shi of tribute rice annually; now the two-tax grain substitution was further set at one million shi, entrusted to the Liang-Zhe military commissioner Han Huang to transport one million shi to East Wei Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Because famine persisted, he also raised the Zhejiang circuits' annual tribute rice from 750,000 to 1,000,000 shi under the two-tax grain levy and charged Liang-Zhe commissioner Han Huang with delivering it to East Wei Bridge;

sentences.zh: 其淮南濠壽旨米、洪潭屯米，委淮南節度使杜亞運送二十萬石至東渭橋。

translations.literal: Huainan, Hao, Shou, and Zhi rice and Hong-Tan garrison rice were entrusted to the Huainan military commissioner Du Ya to transport two hundred thousand shi to East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: while rice from Huainan, Hao, Shou, and Zhi and garrison grain from Hong and Tan were entrusted to Huainan commissioner Du Ya to deliver 200,000 shi to East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 諸道有鹽鐵處，依舊置巡院勾當；

translations.literal: In circuits with salt-iron, inspection offices were to be established as before to manage affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In circuits with salt-iron deposits, local inspection offices were to remain as before;

sentences.zh: 河陰見在米及諸道先付度支、巡院般運在路錢物，委度支依前勾當，其未離本道者，分付觀察使發遣，仍委中書門下年終類例諸道課最聞奏。

translations.literal: Heyin rice on hand and money and goods previously paid to the Revenue Bureau and inspection offices for transport en route were entrusted to the Revenue Bureau to manage as before; what had not yet left the home circuit was divided and entrusted to observation commissioners to dispatch; and the Secretariat and Chancellery were still entrusted at year's end to categorize all circuits' performance and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Heyin grain stores and funds already committed to the Revenue Bureau or en-route transport were left under Revenue Bureau control; goods still within home circuits were assigned to observation commissioners for dispatch; and the Secretariat and Chancellery were to report annual performance rankings by circuit.

sentences.zh: 造與元琇素厚，罷使之後，以鹽鐵之任委之。

translations.literal: Zao and Yuan Xiu had long been close; after abolishing the commissioners, he entrusted the salt-iron duties to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zao and Yuan Xiu were old friends; after abolishing the transport commissioners he gave Yuan Xiu charge of salt-iron affairs.

sentences.zh: 而韓滉方司轉運，朝廷仰給其漕發。

translations.literal: But Han Huang was then managing transport, and the court relied on his grain shipments.
translations.idiomatic: But Han Huang was already running transport, and the court depended on his grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 滉以司務久行，不可遽改。

translations.literal: Huang said the office had long been in operation and could not be suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang argued that the transport system had long been established and could not be abruptly dismantled.

sentences.zh: 德宗復以滉為江淮轉運使，余如造所條奏。

translations.literal: Dezong again made Huang Jiang-Huai transport commissioner; the remainder followed Zao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong therefore reappointed Huang as Jiang-Huai transport commissioner while adopting the rest of Zao's plan.

sentences.zh: 元琇以滉性剛難制，乃復奏江淮轉運，其江南米自江至揚子凡十八里，請滉主之；

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu, because Huang's nature was stubborn and hard to control, again memorialized on Jiang-Huai transport: from the river to Yangzi was eighteen li—he requested Huang oversee it;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, finding Huang ungovernable, proposed splitting Jiang-Huai transport: the eighteen li from the river to Yangzi would fall to Huang;

sentences.zh: 揚子已北，琇主之。

translations.literal: north of Yangzi, Xiu would oversee.
translations.idiomatic: north of Yangzi to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 滉聞之怒，掎摭琇鹽鐵司事論奏。

translations.literal: Huang, hearing of it, grew angry and seized on flaws in Xiu's salt-iron office to memorialize against him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was furious and memorialized against Xiu, dredging up faults in the salt-iron office.

sentences.zh: 德宗不獲已，罷琇判使，轉尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Dezong had no choice; he dismissed Xiu from commissioner adjudication and transferred him to Right Vice Director of State.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong reluctantly removed Xiu from the commission and transferred him to Right Vice Director of State.

sentences.zh: 其年秋初，江淮漕米大至京師，德宗嘉其功，以滉專領度支、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，造所條奏皆改。

translations.literal: That autumn, Jiang-Huai tribute rice largely reached the capital; Dezong praised the achievement and made Huang solely oversee the Revenue Bureau, all circuits' salt-iron transport, and related offices; everything Zao had memorialized was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Early that autumn Jiang-Huai grain reached the capital in force. Dezong praised Huang's success, gave him sole charge of revenue, salt-iron, and transport, and overturned Zao's entire program.

sentences.zh: 物議亦以造所奏雖舉舊典，然凶荒之歲，難為集事，乃罷造知政事，守太子右庶子，貶琇雷州司戶。

translations.literal: Public opinion also held that although Zao's memorial cited old precedents, in a year of famine it was hard to accomplish; Zao was therefore dismissed from government affairs, kept as Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Xiu was demoted to revenue clerk of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that although Zao's reforms invoked ancient precedent, they were impracticable in famine. Zao was removed from the council, kept only as Right Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Yuan Xiu was demoted to revenue clerk in Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 造初奏太銳，及琇改官，憂懼成疾，數月不能視事。

translations.literal: Zao's initial memorial had been too sharp; when Xiu was changed in office, worry and fear became illness, and for months he could not handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's opening proposals had been too aggressive; when Xiu was demoted he fell ill with anxiety and for months could not attend to business.

sentences.zh: 明年九月卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following ninth month at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 關播，字務元，衛州汲人也。

translations.literal: Guan Bo, style name Wuyuan, was a native of Ji in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo, courtesy name Wuyuan, was from Ji in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 鄧景山為淮南節度使，闢為從事，累授衛佐評事，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: When Deng Jingshan was Huainan Military Commissioner, he recruited him as staff member, repeatedly appointed him Wei Assistant Reviewer, and promoted him to Right Supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Jingshan served as Huainan military commissioner, he recruited Bo as staff aide, later appointed him Wei Assistant Reviewer, and promoted him to Right Supplementation.

sentences.zh: 善言物理，尤精釋氏之學。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discussing natural principle and especially versed in Buddhist learning.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke well on natural philosophy and was especially learned in Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，神策軍使王駕鶴妻關氏以播與同宗，深遇之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, the wife of the Shence Army commander Wang Jiahe, née Guan, because Bo was of the same clan, treated him with deep favor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Lady Guan, wife of Shence Army commander Wang Jiahe, treated Bo with great favor as a clansman.

sentences.zh: 元載惡其交往，出為河南府兵曹，攝職數縣，皆有政能。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai resented this association and sent him out as Henan Prefecture military staff officer; acting in several counties, he showed administrative ability in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, disliking this connection, posted him to Henan as military staff officer. Acting in several counties, he proved capable in each.

sentences.zh: 陳少游領浙東、淮南，又闢為判官，歷檢校金部員外，攝滁州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Shaoyou held Zhedong and Huainan and again recruited him as staff judge; he served as Acting Vice Minister of the Gold Bureau and Acting Prefect of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Shaoyou governed Zhedong and Huainan, he again recruited Bo as staff judge. Bo rose to Acting Vice Minister of the Gold Bureau and Acting Prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李靈曜阻兵，跋扈於梁汴。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao obstructed with arms and was overbearing in Liang and Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao defied the court with military force and lorded it over Liang and Bian.

sentences.zh: 少游自總兵鎮淮上，所在盜賊峰起。

translations.literal: Shaoyou himself commanded troops garrisoning the Huai region, and wherever he went bandits rose like peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou commanded troops on the Huai, and bandits swarmed wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 播調閱州兵，令其守備。
