translations.literal: Bo inspected and reviewed the prefectural troops and ordered them to guard and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Bo inspected the prefectural troops and put them on guard.

sentences.zh: 又為政清淨簡惠，既無盜賊，人甚安之。

translations.literal: Moreover his governance was pure, quiet, simple, and benevolent; once there were no bandits, the people were greatly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was clean, simple, and humane. Banditry ceased, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞知政事，薦播為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Yang Wan and Chang Gun handled state affairs and recommended Bo as Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wan and Chang Gun held power, they recommended Bo for Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 德宗登極，湖南山洞中有王國良者，聚眾為盜，令播往宣撫之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, in a mountain cave in Hunan there was one Wang Guoliang who gathered a crowd and became a bandit; he ordered Bo to go and proclaim and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, a bandit named Wang Guoliang gathered followers in a Hunan mountain cave. The emperor sent Bo to offer him amnesty.

sentences.zh: 臨行，召對於別殿，上問政理之要，播奏云：「為政之本，需求有道賢人，乃可得理。

translations.literal: Before departure he was summoned for audience in a separate hall; the emperor asked the essentials of governing well, and Bo memorialized saying: "The root of governing is to seek men of the Way who are worthy—only then can order be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Dezong summoned him to a side hall and asked the essentials of good government. Bo replied, "The foundation of rule is to find worthy men of principle—only then can the realm be governed."

sentences.zh: 」上謂播云：「朕下詔求賢良，當躬新閱試，亦遣使臣黜陟，廣加搜訪聞薦，擢其能者用之，冀以傅理。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Bo: "We have issued edicts seeking the worthy and good, and will personally conduct new examinations; we also dispatch envoys for promotion and demotion, broadly search, hear recommendations, and elevate the capable for use, hoping thereby to assist in governing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have issued edicts seeking talent, will personally examine candidates, and send envoys to promote and demote, searching widely and elevating the able—hoping thereby to govern well."

sentences.zh: 」播奏曰：「下詔求賢黜陟舉薦，唯得求名詞之士，安有有道賢人肯隨牒舉選乎？

translations.literal: Bo memorialized saying: "Issuing edicts to seek the worthy, promoting and demoting and recommending—one obtains only men who seek fame and rhetoric; how could there be worthy men of the Way willing to follow documents and enter selection?"
translations.idiomatic: Bo replied, "Edicts, examinations, and recommendations only produce men who chase reputation. What man of true worth would submit to the examination rolls?"

sentences.zh: 」上悅其言，謂播曰：「卿且使去，回日當與卿論政事。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with his words and said to Bo: "You, sir, go on your mission for now; on your return day we shall discuss state affairs with you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "Go on your mission for now. When you return we shall discuss affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 」播又奏曰：「臣今奏詔招撫，國良不受命，臣請便宣恩命，語鄰境速出兵翦除。

translations.literal: Bo again memorialized saying: "Your subject now carries an edict to offer amnesty and pacification; if Guoliang does not accept the command, your subject requests to proclaim the gracious order on the spot and tell neighboring jurisdictions to speed troops to cut him down."
translations.idiomatic: Bo added, "If Guoliang refuses the amnesty, I ask leave to proclaim the imperial grace at once and urge neighboring commands to send troops and destroy him."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言深合朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words deeply accord with Our mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your words accord perfectly with my intent."

sentences.zh: 」使回，改兵部員外，遷河中少尹。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Junior Vice Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Junior Vice Governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 建中初，張鎰為河中少尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Zhang Yi was Junior Vice Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianzhong reign, Zhang Yi was junior vice governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 鎰尋入相，二年七月，遷播給事中。

translations.literal: Yi soon entered the chancellery; in the seventh month of the second year, Bo was promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yi soon became chief minister. In the seventh month of the second year Bo was promoted to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 舊例，諸司甲庫，皆是胥吏掌知，為弊頗久，播始建議並以士人知之，至今稱當。

translations.literal: By old custom, the document archives of all bureaus were all managed by clerks, which had been a abuse for quite long; Bo was the first to propose that all be managed by literati, and to this day it is called appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: By long custom every bureau's archives had been run by clerks, a source of chronic abuse. Bo was first to propose placing them under literati, a reform still praised as sound.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎、奉迎皇太后副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and Deputy Commissioner for Welcoming the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and deputy commissioner for welcoming the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 盧杞以播柔緩，冀其易制，驟稱薦之。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, because Bo was gentle and slow, hoped he would be easy to control, and suddenly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, finding Bo mild and pliable, hoped to control him easily and suddenly praised him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部侍郎，轉刑部尚書、知刪定。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel and transferred to Minister of Justice, with charge of editorial deletion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel, then Minister of Justice with charge of legal revision.

sentences.zh: 奏上元中，詔擇古今名將十人於武成王廟配享，如文宣王廟之儀。

translations.literal: He memorialized that in the Shangyuan era an edict had selected ten famous generals ancient and modern for secondary sacrifice in the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, following the rites of the Temple of the Literary Propagation King.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that in the Shangyuan era an edict had named ten famous generals for secondary sacrifice in the Temple of the Martial Accomplishment King, following the model of Confucius's temple.

sentences.zh: 播以「太公古稱大賢，今其下稱亞聖，於義不安。

translations.literal: Bo held that "the Grand Duke in antiquity was called a great worthy; now beneath him they are called sub-sages—in principle this is improper."
translations.idiomatic: Bo argued that "the Grand Duke was called a great sage in antiquity; to rank others beneath him as sub-sages is improper in principle."

sentences.zh: 又孔子十哲，皆是當時弟子，今所擇名將，年代不同，於義既乖，於事又失。

translations.literal: Moreover Confucius's Ten Wise Ones were all disciples of his own time; the famous generals now chosen are of different eras—in principle it already conflicts, and in practice it is also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's Ten Wise Ones were all his own disciples, whereas the chosen generals belong to different ages—the principle is wrong and the practice mistaken.

sentences.zh: 臣請刪去名將配享之儀及十哲之稱。

translations.literal: Your subject requests deletion of the rite of famous generals in secondary sacrifice and the title of Ten Wise Ones.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the generals' secondary sacrifice and the title Ten Wise Ones both be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 建中三年十月，拜銀青光祿大夫、中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jianzhong he was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling Worthies and Hall for Venerating Culture, and Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianzhong 3 (782) he was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister, Grand Academician of the imperial libraries, and Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 時政事決在盧杞，播但斂衽取容而已。

translations.literal: At the time state affairs were decided by Lu Qi; Bo only drew in his lapels and sought to please.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs rested with Lu Qi; Bo merely folded his hands and sought to please.

sentences.zh: 乏於知人之鑑，好大言虛誕者，播必悅而親信之。

translations.literal: Lacking the mirror of knowing men, he was fond of those who spoke great words and empty absurdities; Bo was sure to be pleased and personally trust them.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked discernment in judging men and delighted in boastful charlatans, whom he always favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 有李元平、陶公達、張愻、劉承誡，皆言談詭妄，讠誇大可立功名，亦有微材薄藝。

translations.literal: There were Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Xun, and Liu Chengjie—all whose talk was bizarre and delusive, boasting that great merit and fame could be established, and who also had slight talent and thin arts.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Li Yuanping, Tao Gongda, Zhang Xun, and Liu Chengjie—all given to wild talk and boasting of great deeds, though they possessed only slight talents.

sentences.zh: 播累奏雲元平等皆可將相也，請閱試用之，上以為然，以元平為補闕。

translations.literal: Bo repeatedly memorialized saying Yuanping and the others could all become generals and chief ministers, and requested examination and trial employment; the emperor thought it so, and made Yuanping Supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: Bo repeatedly memorialized that Yuanping and the others were fit for general and ministerial rank and asked that they be tested. The emperor agreed and appointed Yuanping Supplementation.

sentences.zh: 會淮西節度李希烈叛亂，上以汝州要鎮，令選擇刺史。

translations.literal: It happened that Huainan West Military Commissioner Li Xilie rebelled; the emperor, because Ruzhou was a key garrison, ordered selection of a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie of Huainan West rebelled, the emperor, deeming Ruzhou a critical post, ordered a prefect chosen.

sentences.zh: 播薦元平為汝州刺史，尋加檢校吏部郎中、汝州別駕，知州事。

translations.literal: Bo recommended Yuanping as Prefect of Ruzhou; before long he was additionally made Acting Director of the Personnel Bureau, Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, and charged with prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bo recommended Yuanping as prefect of Ruzhou, then additionally as Acting Director of the Personnel Bureau and vice prefect in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元平至州旬日，為希烈所擒，汝州陷賊，中外哂之。

translations.literal: Within ten days of Yuanping's arrival at the prefecture he was captured by Xilie; Ruzhou fell to the rebels, and court and countryside sneered.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of reaching Ruzhou, Yuanping was captured by Xilie and the prefecture fell. Court and country alike mocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 由是公達等未克任用。

translations.literal: Because of this Gongda and the others could not be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gongda and the others were never appointed.

sentences.zh: 播與盧杞等從駕幸奉天，既而杞、白志貞等並貶黜，播尚知政事，中外囂然，以為不可，遂罷相，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Bo followed Lu Qi and others in attending the emperor to Fengtian; afterward Qi, Bai Zhizhen, and others were all demoted and dismissed, but Bo still handled state affairs; court and countryside were in uproar, thinking it impossible, and he was therefore removed from the chancellery and made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Bo followed Lu Qi and the court to Fengtian. After Qi and Bai Zhizhen were demoted, Bo still held power, provoking widespread outrage. He was removed from the chancellery and made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 大臣韋倫等泣於朝曰：「宰相不能謀猷翊贊，以至今日，而尚為尚書，可痛心也！」

translations.literal: The great minister Wei Lun and others wept in court saying: "The chief minister could not plan and assist to support, leading to today—and he is still Minister! How heartbreaking!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wei Lun and others wept in open court, "The chief minister could neither plan nor assist, and brought us to this pass—yet he remains a minister! It is heartbreaking!"

sentences.zh: 貞元四年，回紇請和親，以咸安公主出降可汗，令播以本官加檢校右僕射、兼御史大夫，持節充送咸安公主及冊可汗使，奉使往來，皆清儉謹慎，蕃人悅之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan the Uyghurs requested marriage alliance; the Princess of Xian'an was sent down to marry the qaghan; Bo was ordered with his original office additionally made Acting Right Vice Director, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner with credentials as envoy escorting the Princess of Xian'an and enfeoffing the qaghan; on missions back and forth he was all pure, frugal, and cautious, and the foreigners were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 4 (788) the Uyghurs sought a marriage alliance and Princess Xian'an was sent to wed the qaghan. Bo was appointed Acting Right Vice Director and Censor-in-Chief with credentials as envoy escorting the princess and investing the qaghan. On every mission he was frugal and careful, winning the foreigners' esteem.

sentences.zh: 使回，遷兵部尚書，固辭疾，請罷官，改太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs, firmly declined on grounds of illness, requested dismissal from office, and was changed to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs but pleaded illness, asked to leave office, and was granted retirement as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 播致仕之後，減去僮僕車騎，閉關守靜，不縈外事，士君子重之。

translations.literal: After Bo retired he reduced servants and carriages and horses, shut his gates and kept quiet, and did not entangle himself in outside affairs; men of honor esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he reduced his household and retinue, shut his gates, and kept aloof from public affairs. Men of honor respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年正月卒，時年七十九，廢朝一日，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged seventy-nine at the time; the court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of Zhenyuan 13 (797) at the age of seventy-nine. The court suspended audiences for a day and posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 李元平者，宗室子。

translations.literal: Li Yuanping was a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanping was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 始為湖南觀察使蕭復判官，試大理評事。

translations.literal: He first served as staff judge to Hunan Observation Commissioner Xiao Fu, and was tried as Grand Court Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as staff judge to Hunan observation commissioner Xiao Fu and held the provisional title of Grand Court Reviewer.

sentences.zh: 性疏傲，敢大言，好論兵，天下賢士大夫無可其意者，以是人多銜怒。

translations.literal: By nature he was coarse and arrogant, dared great words, loved discussing warfare; there were no worthy scholar-officials under Heaven who met his approval, and therefore many harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He was coarse and arrogant, spoke boldly, and loved to discourse on warfare. No worthy official in the realm met his standard, and many bore him resentment.

sentences.zh: 關播奇重之，許以將帥。

translations.literal: Guan Bo regarded him as extraordinary and valued him, promising him the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Bo thought him remarkable and promised him a general's command.

sentences.zh: 時希烈反叛，朝廷以汝州與賊接壤，刺史韋光裔懦弱不任職，播乃盛稱元平，特召見，超左補闕，不數日，擢為檢校吏部郎中，兼汝州別駕，知州事。

translations.literal: At the time Xilie rebelled; the court, because Ruzhou bordered the rebels, and Prefect Wei Guangyi was weak and incompetent, Bo then greatly praised Yuanping; he was specially summoned for audience, leap-promoted to Left Supplementation, and within several days was elevated to Acting Director of the Personnel Bureau, concurrent Vice Prefect of Ruzhou, charged with prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie rebelled, Ruzhou bordered rebel territory and Prefect Wei Guangyi proved incompetent. Bo lavishly praised Yuanping, who was specially summoned, leap-promoted to Left Supplementation, and within days made Acting Director of the Personnel Bureau and vice prefect of Ruzhou in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既至部，募工徒繕理郛郭，希烈乃使勇士應募，執役板築，凡入數百人，元平不之覺。

translations.literal: Once he reached his post he recruited laborers to repair the outer walls; Xilie then sent brave warriors to answer the recruitment, performing corvée and rammed-earth work; in all several hundred men entered, and Yuanping did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he recruited laborers to repair the walls. Xilie sent warriors to enlist as laborers—several hundred in all—and Yuanping never noticed.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣偽將李克誠以數百騎突至其城，先應募執役者應於內，縛元平馳去。

translations.literal: Xilie dispatched the false general Li Kecheng with several hundred horsemen to burst upon his city; those who had first answered recruitment and performed corvée responded from within, bound Yuanping and galloped away with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent his general Li Kecheng with several hundred horsemen to storm the city. The enlisted laborers opened the gates from within, seized Yuanping, and rode off with him.

sentences.zh: 既見希烈，遺下污地。

translations.literal: Once he saw Xilie, he soiled the ground below.
translations.idiomatic: When brought before Xilie, he fouled himself on the ground.

sentences.zh: 希烈見其無須眇小，戲謂克誠曰：「使汝取李元平，何得將元平兒來？

translations.literal: Xilie, seeing that he was beardless and small, jested to Kecheng saying: "I sent you to fetch Li Yuanping—how did you bring Yuanping's boy?"
translations.idiomatic: Xilie, seeing he was beardless and slight, joked to Kecheng, "I sent you for Li Yuanping—why have you brought his son?"

sentences.zh: 」因嫚罵曰：「盲宰相使汝當我，何待我淺耶！

translations.literal: He then reviled him saying: "A blind chief minister sent you to face me—why do you treat me so lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: He then cursed him, "A blind chief minister sent you against me—do you take me so lightly!"

sentences.zh: 」偽署為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was falsely appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie gave him the false title of Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 播聞元平得用，仍欺於人曰：「李生功業濟矣。

translations.literal: Bo heard that Yuanping had been employed and still deceived people saying: "Master Li's merit and achievement are about to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Bo heard Yuanping had been appointed, he still told people, "Master Li's great deeds are about to succeed."

sentences.zh: 」言必能覆希烈而建功也。

translations.literal: He said he would surely be able to overthrow Xilie and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Yuanping would surely overthrow Xilie and win glory.

sentences.zh: 居無何，希烈用為宰相，或告其有二者，乃斷一指以自誓。

translations.literal: Before long Xilie employed him as chief minister; someone reported that he had divided loyalties, and he cut off a finger to swear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xilie made him chief minister. When someone accused him of divided loyalty, he cut off a finger to swear his faith.

sentences.zh: 希烈既死，或有人言在賊中微有謀慮，貸死流於珍州。

translations.literal: After Xilie died, someone said that while among the rebels he had slight plotting and counsel; his death was spared and he was exiled to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie's death someone reported that he had shown some counsel among the rebels. His life was spared and he was exiled to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 會赦得歸剡中，浙東觀察使皇甫政表聞其到，以發上怒，復流賀州而死。

translations.literal: When an amnesty allowed him to return to Kuai, Zhedong Observation Commissioner Huangfu Zheng memorialized reporting his arrival, which provoked the emperor's anger; he was again exiled to He Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty allowed him to return to Kuai, but Zhedong observation commissioner Huangfu Zheng reported his arrival, provoking the emperor's wrath. He was exiled again to Hezhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：蒸嘗礿祀，前王制以奉先；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Summer and winter offerings and border sacrifices—the former kings instituted them to serve the ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Summer and winter offerings and border sacrifices were instituted by the ancient kings to honor the ancestors;

sentences.zh: 怪力亂神，宣聖鄙而不語。

translations.literal: strange force, disordering spirits—the Propagating Sage despised them and did not speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: but strange powers and spirits disturbing order—the Sage himself despised and would not discuss.

sentences.zh: 凡雲左道，固有舊章。

translations.literal: Whenever one speaks of heterodox ways, there are certainly old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox ways have always been forbidden by statute.

sentences.zh: 玙假於鬼神，乃至將相，既處代天之位，爰滋亂政之源。

translations.literal: Yu borrowed from ghosts and spirits and even reached general and chief minister; once he occupied the position of acting for Heaven, he thereby nourished the source of disordered government.
translations.idiomatic: Yu invoked ghosts and spirits to rise to general and chief minister; once he stood in the place of Heaven's deputy, he became a fountainhead of misgovernment.

sentences.zh: 國禎妖人疑眾，妄恢其祀典；

translations.literal: Guozhen the sorcerer deluded the multitude and wantonly expanded the sacrificial canon;
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen the sorcerer misled the people and wantonly expanded the state cult;

sentences.zh: 梁鎮正士抗疏，方悟其上心。

translations.literal: the upright man Liang Zhen submitted a defiant memorial, and only then was the emperor's mind awakened.
translations.idiomatic: only when the upright Liang Zhen submitted his defiant memorial did the emperor's mind awaken.

sentences.zh: 泌見可進而知難退，足為高率智辯之士；

translations.literal: Bi, seeing when he could advance and knowing when difficulty required withdrawal, was sufficient to be a man of lofty bearing, wisdom, and eloquence;
translations.idiomatic: Bi knew when to advance and when to withdraw—truly a man of lofty wisdom and eloquence;

sentences.zh: 居相位而談鬼神，乃見狂妄浮薄之蹤。

translations.literal: yet occupying the chancellery while discussing ghosts and spirits showed the traces of arrogant delusion and frivolity.
translations.idiomatic: yet to hold the chancellery while discoursing on spirits revealed arrogant frivolity.

sentences.zh: 《王制》云：「執左道以亂政，殺。

translations.literal: The Royal Regulations say: "Those who wield heterodox ways to disorder government—kill."
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Regulations state, "Whoever employs heterodox ways to subvert government shall be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」寧無畏乎！

translations.literal: Was there truly no fear!
translations.idiomatic: Did they feel no fear?

sentences.zh: 繁之醜行，棄於當時，竟陷非辜，諒由素履。

translations.literal: Fan's ugly conduct was abandoned by his contemporaries; he ultimately fell into undeserved guilt—no doubt because of his lifelong conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's vile conduct earned the scorn of his age; that he died unjustly was no doubt the fruit of his lifelong ways.

sentences.zh: 造為臣得禮，蒞事非能；

translations.literal: Zao as minister obtained ritual propriety but was not capable in undertaking affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zao understood propriety as a minister but lacked capacity in office;

sentences.zh: 播居位取容，舉人敗事。

translations.literal: Bo in office sought to please; in raising men he ruined affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bo sought only to please in office and ruined affairs through his appointments.

sentences.zh: 皆非國器，咸歷台司，失人者亡，國其危矣。

translations.literal: None were vessels of state; all passed through high offices—those who lose men perish, and the state was indeed in peril.
translations.idiomatic: None were fit to govern the state, yet all held high office. When rulers lose the right men, the state perishes—and the realm was indeed in peril.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：玙、泌、造、播，俱非相材。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yu, Bi, Zao, and Bo were all not material for chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Yu, Bi, Zao, and Bo were none of them fit for the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 國禎左道，梁生直哉！

translations.literal: Guozhen's heterodox way; Master Liang was upright indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen walked the heterodox path; Master Liang was upright indeed!
